subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar intentionally treat its shared persistent config as an opt-in local command-execution surface in both the menu-bar app and CLI?
rationale: The implementation is bounded and well-proven, but automation cannot decide whether background app events should execute arbitrary user-configured binaries as a permanent product and security contract.

options.title: Sponsor guarded app and CLI hooks
options.body: Accept the execution boundary after the argv editor is made lossless and the config threat model is documented and tested.

options.title: Limit hooks to foreground CLI use
options.body: Keep event testing or polling in explicit CLI workflows and avoid automatic command execution from the long-running app.

options.title: Decline local execution hooks
options.body: Keep CodexBar observability-only and direct automation users to polling existing localhost or CLI data surfaces.

recommendation.title: Sponsor guarded app and CLI hooks
recommendation.body: Accept the execution boundary after the argv editor is made lossless and the config threat model is documented and tested.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is the best available authority for accepting a new persistent local execution contract.
